claims.text: Refractory HEA and Cu powders tend to segregate during conventional processing because of their positive mixing enthalpy.
SPS can enable large-scale reactive consolidation of blended refractory HEA and Cu powders.
SPS can overcome the positive heat of mixing between refractory HEAs and Cu.
SPS quickly forms transient interfacial phases that stabilize the microstructure.
SPS applies rapid pulsed electrical heating and uniaxial pressure to consolidate the powder blend.
A fast heating rate and short dwell time minimize uncontrolled diffusion during consolidation.
Fine transient interfacial layers or localized diffusion zones mediate bonding between refractory particles and Cu.
The interfacial layers limit extensive intermixing between the refractory particles and Cu.
Rapid and localized SPS heating enhances diffusion at particle interfaces.
Enhanced interfacial diffusion permits a controlled reaction that produces metastable phases.
The controlled interfacial reaction produces a coherent, fine-scale composite microstructure despite the positive heat of mixing.
SPS will produce a homogeneous distribution of Cu within the refractory HEA matrix.
The SPS-processed composite will exhibit minimal phase segregation.
The SPS-processed composite will have improved mechanical properties compared with conventionally processed samples.
The SPS-processed composite will have improved irradiation resistance compared with conventionally processed samples.
Conventional sintering or casting typically causes significant phase separation or undesirable intermetallic formation in refractory HEA–Cu systems.
The success of SPS depends on temperature, pressure, and heating rate.
Deviations from suitable SPS parameters may cause inadequate diffusion control and phase inhomogeneity.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis affirmatively claims that SPS will enable large-scale consolidation, while the boundary and uncertainty fields state that scale-up is challenging and that scalability for large reactor components remains unquantified.
